senses.sense_definition: A brass musical instrument with a flared bell and valves, played by blowing through a cup-shaped mouthpiece.

examples.text: She learned to play the <w>trumpet</w> in the school marching band.
The royal herald sounded a brass <w>trumpet</w> to announce their arrival.

senses.sense_definition: The loud, harsh cry made by an elephant or a similar animal.

examples.text: We were startled by the sudden <w>trumpet</w> of an elephant in the trees.
The large bull gave a powerful <w>trumpet</w> before moving toward the river.

senses.sense_definition: A musician who plays the trumpet.

examples.text: The <w>trumpets</w> were asked to stand at the rear of the orchestra pit.
The conductor gave a cue directly to the first <w>trumpet</w>.

senses.sense_definition: A plant or flower having a trumpet-like, flared shape.

examples.text: Golden <w>trumpets</w> bloomed along the stone wall throughout the summer.
The vine is known for producing a large yellow <w>trumpet</w> that attracts hummingbirds.

senses.sense_definition: A powerful reed stop on a pipe organ producing a tone resembling that of a brass trumpet.

examples.text: The organist engaged the <w>trumpet</w> stop to announce the final hymn.
The cathedral organ features a loud horizontal <w>trumpet</w> over the entrance.

senses.sense_definition: A highway interchange design incorporating at least one loop ramp resembling a trumpet.

examples.text: Traffic slowed as vehicles navigated the tight curve of the <w>trumpet</w> interchange.
Planners replaced the intersection with a modern <w>trumpet</w> to improve vehicle flow.

senses.sense_definition: A flared pipe or funnel used to guide flexible material such as yarn into a machine.

examples.text: Thread the synthetic fibers carefully through the metal <w>trumpet</w> before spinning.
The guide <w>trumpet</w> ensures the yarn enters the knitting cylinder evenly.

senses.sense_definition: A person or agency that publicly extols, proclaims, or spreads praise.

examples.text: He acted as the willing <w>trumpet</w> of his patron's supposed generosity.
The newspaper served as a constant <w>trumpet</w> for the regime.

traits.comment: Used in archaic or literary contexts

senses.sense_definition: An ardent political supporter of Donald Trump.

examples.text: Commentators debated whether the online group was composed of genuine <w>trumpets</w> or automated bots.
He identified as an outspoken <w>trumpet</w> on various social media platforms.

senses.sense_definition: To play the musical instrument known as a trumpet.

examples.text: He spent his weekends busking and <w>trumpeting</w> on the busy subway platform.
She began <w>trumpeting</w> softly to test the acoustics of the hall.

senses.sense_definition: To proclaim, announce, or celebrate something loudly and publicly.

examples.text: The company was eager to <w>trumpet</w> its record profits to the public.
Politicians often <w>trumpet</w> their achievements right before an upcoming election.

senses.sense_definition: To utter the characteristic loud, piercing cry of an elephant.

examples.text: We watched the mother elephant <w>trumpet</w> to call her calf back.
The agitated herd began to <w>trumpet</w> loudly across the open savanna.

senses.sense_definition: To make or emit a loud, blaring sound.

examples.text: Loud rock music <w>trumpeted</w> through the open windows of the car.
Car horns <w>trumpeted</w> continuously in the heavy morning traffic.

senses.sense_definition: To utter a loud, piercing cry resembling that of an elephant or brass horn.

examples.text: A solitary crane <w>trumpeted</w> overhead as it flew toward the lake.
The wild swan <w>trumpeted</w> across the misty marsh to warn its mate.
